title: Full beat-by-beat script: overnight SSH triage on jump01 (Terminal.app + Google Sheets + Google Docs in Firefox)

steps.title: Opener
steps.window: The recorder card, then the Goal doc (Firefox)
steps.do: Read the opener off the recorder card, cursor still, with no pause after "in mind". During the last words start sliding the cursor toward the yellow minimise button of the Goal doc, then minimise the recorder. Keep the cursor sliding up and left from the Goal doc text toward the yellow minimise button at the top left of its window while you speak, with no pause after "blocked". Click the yellow minimise button at the top left of the Goal doc window, on the first word, "Minimising", and narrate the rest as it happens.
say: "Step 1: I will be beginning my task soon. Here is the workflow I have in mind."
"I'm going through last night's failed SSH logins on jump01, to decide what gets blocked."
"Minimising the Goal doc: my cursor's on the yellow button, top left of its window, and one left click clears it, so the screen's free."

cursor > up-left > Goal doc > jump01 failed SSH logins > what gets blocked

steps.title: Terminal first look
steps.window: Dock, then the Terminal window
steps.do: Move the cursor down to the Dock on the left edge, onto the Terminal icon, and click it to bring Terminal forward (it is already open in Documents/Project). Pause 1 s after "a click brings it up". Look at the Terminal window: the "$ " prompt in Documents/Project, 16 pt. Type wc -l auth-jump01.log at the prompt while speaking, with no pause, then press Return. Read the output line: 59 auth-jump01.log. Hold on to 59 for the import check.
say: "Step 2: okay, Terminal first. Down the left Dock to its icon, and a click brings it up."
"Alright, Terminal's up, with the prompt in Documents, Project."
"Typing w c, space, dash l, then auth-jump01.log, a raw line count to check the import against, and Return."
"59 lines in auth-jump01.log, so that's my import check."

Terminal up > prompt > Documents, Project
type > wc -l > auth-jump01.log > Return
read > 59 lines > import check

steps.title: Count failed and unknown-account logins
steps.window: Terminal window
steps.do: Type grep -c "Failed password" auth-jump01.log at the prompt while speaking, with no pause, then press Return. Read the count on the next line: 53. Type grep -c "invalid user" auth-jump01.log on the next prompt while speaking, with no pause, then press Return. Read the count on the next line: 14. Rest the cursor on the two counts, 53 and 14, and say what they mean for the pivot check.
steps.type:
grep -c "Failed password" auth-jump01.log
grep -c "invalid user" auth-jump01.log
say: "Step 3: the failures. Typing grep dash c, Failed password in quotes, and the log name, then Return, for a number to hit."
"It says 53, so that's 53 Failed password lines to match."
"Below that, typing the same grep dash c but with invalid user in quotes, then Return, to count accounts that don't exist."
"14 invalid user lines, so someone's guessing usernames, not just fumbling a password."
"So both counts are my bar: if the pivot isn't 53, the import's wrong, and I'd recheck."

read > 53 > Failed password lines
type > grep -c > invalid user > Return
read > 14 > invalid user > guessing usernames
read > 53 and 14 > pivot must say 53 > else recheck

steps.title: List successful logins
steps.window: Terminal window
steps.do: Type grep 'Accepted' auth-jump01.log (Accepted in single quotes) while speaking, with no pause, then press Return. Read the six Accepted lines: publickey at 00:30:00, 07:05:00 and 07:40:00; password at 03:52:34 for svc_backup from 192.0.2.77, 04:20:34 for jsmith from 198.51.100.140 and 06:04:12 for ops.admin from 10.20.4.11. Rest the cursor on line 2: 03:52:34, Accepted password for svc_backup from 192.0.2.77, port 62963, and say you will come back to it. Look over the password lines and say why those IPs are compared in the sheet rather than blocked from Terminal.
say: "Step 4: who got in. Below that, typing grep, Accepted in single quotes, the log name, and Return, to list logins."
"Six Accepted lines, three publickey and three password, and the password ones are my focus."
"Second line, 03:52:34, Accepted password for svc_backup from 192.0.2.77. Hmm, I'll come back to that."
"An IP that failed, then got in, needs its account checked, so I'll compare those in the sheet first."

steps.title: Import the log export and check it
steps.window: Google Sheets (Firefox) > Import files dialog > Mac file picker
steps.do: Move up to the Sheets menu bar, to File on the far left, and left click it. Pause 1 s after "a left click opens it". Move down the File menu to Import and select it. Pause 1 s after "select it". In the Import files box click the Upload tab along the top (the file is on the Mac, not in Drive). Pause 1 s after "click the Upload tab". Click Browse in the middle of the Upload tab. Pause 1 s after "I press it". In the Mac file picker click Documents once in the left sidebar. Pause 1 s after "one click". Double-click Project in the list on the right. Pause 1 s after "double-click it". Click auth-jump01-excerpt.csv once to select it; say "excerpt", not the extension. Pause 1 s after "selects it". Click Open at the bottom right of the picker. Pause 1 s after "a click". In the Import file box, under Import location, click Replace current sheet. Pause 1 s after "I pick it". Click Import data at the bottom of the box. Pause 1 s after "I press it". Wait while the rows fill in, staying silent for up to 4 s. Read row 1: timestamp, host, event, user, invalid_user, src_ip, decision. src_ip is column F, the filter column. Look over at column G, decision: it is empty all the way down. Hold Command and press Down to jump to the bottom of the data, while speaking, with no pause. Read the last row number on the left: 60, timestamp 07:40:00. Check: 60 minus the header row is 59, and Terminal said 59 lines. They match, so the import dropped nothing. Hold Command and press Up to return to the top row, while speaking, with no pause.

"In the Import location list, Replace current sheet, and I pick it, since this sheet's blank already."
"Bottom of the box, Import data, and I press it to bring the rows in."
"Waiting a second while the rows fill in."
"Checking the import. Row 1 reads timestamp, host, event, user, invalid user, src ip, decision, so src ip is column F."
"Over in column G, decision, it's empty all the way down, and I'll fill that in myself."
"Holding Command and pressing Down, the last row number on the left is 60, timestamped 07:40:00."
"Sixty minus the header is 59, and Terminal said 59 lines. They match, so the import dropped nothing."

steps.title: Build the pivot: rows, columns, values
steps.window: Google Sheets: Pivot Table 1, pivot editor
steps.do: In the editor on the right, click the Add button beside Rows. Pause 1 s after "a click adds IPs". In the list that drops down, move to src_ip and click it. Pause 1 s after "click it". Move further down to Columns and left click its Add button. Pause 1 s after "a left click". In the list, select event. Pause 1 s after "select it". On the Columns card, click the Show totals checkbox to untick it. Pause 1 s after "with a click". Read across row 2 of the pivot: B Accepted password, C Accepted publickey, D Failed password. Move down to Values and click its Add button. Pause 1 s after "and I click". In the list that opens, pick event. Pause 1 s after "pick event". Look lower on the value card at the Summarize by box to see what it is set to. If it says COUNTA go to the next line; if it says SUM, skip to the line after. If it already shows COUNTA, leave it as it is. Only if it shows SUM: click the Summarize by dropdown, move down to COUNTA and click it. Pause 1 s after "COUNTA and click it". Say why COUNTA fits: each line is one attempt, and it counts the text entries. Read the grid on the left: the counts fill in, with a Grand Total on row 9.
